name: Freelance graphic designer (contests and 1-to-1 projects)
summary: Apply to join 99designs as a designer, then compete in client design contests or take paid 1-to-1 projects such as logos and branding.
whatYouDo: Once accepted, you either enter contests, where many designers submit concepts for one client brief (logo, packaging, social graphics) and only the chosen winner is paid, or you work directly with clients on 1-to-1 projects at a price you set. Your Entry, Mid or Top level controls which contests you can enter and the fee you pay.
appeal: Free to sign up, and clients come to the platform, so you do less self-marketing than going solo
Platform fees fall as you move up levels: 15% at Entry, 10% at Mid and 5% at Top on 1-to-1 projects
A way to build a portfolio and client relationships that can continue as 1-to-1 work
watchOuts: Contests are speculative: losing entries aren't paid, and a study of about 38,000 contests found a large share of designers never win a single contest
One paid winner can face hundreds of other entries (TechCrunch)
Acceptance is competitive. A curation team reviews applications, and after two declined attempts you are declined permanently
Entry-level designers can only enter the lower-priced Bronze and Silver contest packages (third-party summary)
Fees: a 15–5% platform fee depending on level, plus a $100 introduction fee for each new client, spread over that client's first $500
Payouts go only through Hyperwallet since January 2026
A March 2026 Trustpilot reviewer said most of the entries they received were AI-generated (anecdotal). 99designs says it has systems to catch rule-breaking designs
Job Bank rates the 2025–2027 outlook for graphic designers and illustrators as Very limited in Ontario, so competition for design work is high
No source names Canada as an eligible designer country. Eligibility is inferred from the platform's worldwide designer base

training.notes: No platform training found. Professional design-software skills and a strong portfolio are expected.

compensation.notes: No official designer earnings figures found. Third-party sites list client logo-contest prices from US$249 (Bronze) to US$1,050 (Platinum); one critical review estimates the winner receives roughly 60% of the contest fee (unverified). 1-to-1 project prices are set by the designer.

reliability.notes: Contest income depends on winning against many entrants. Academic study of about 38,000 contests: a few designers win consistently and many never win.

fees: Platform fee on 1-to-1 projects: 15% (Entry), 10% (Mid) or 5% (Top level). A $100 introduction fee per new client, spread over that client's first $500 in charges. Free to sign up.
applicationSteps: Prepare a portfolio of your best design work
Set up a Hyperwallet account (required to complete the application)
Submit the designer application for curation review (two attempts allowed)
If accepted at Entry level, enter Bronze or Silver contests or offer 1-to-1 projects, and request a level review after 6 months of activity
fitsIf: You already have solid design skills and a portfolio and can afford to do unpaid contest entries while building a reputation.
notFitIf: You're new to design, need dependable income, or object to doing unpaid speculative work.

sources.title: How does 99designs' application process work?
sources.notes: Search summary: all new designers must apply; a Hyperwallet account is required to complete the application; the Designer Curation team reviews against quality standards and acceptance is highly competitive; two attempts before permanent decline; approved designers placed at Entry, Mid or Top level. Page not opened.

sources.title: What is a platform fee?
sources.notes: Search summary: free to sign up; designer platform fee of 15% (Entry), 10% (Mid) or 5% (Top) per project; a $100 introduction fee spread over a client's first $500; client pays a separate 5% fee. Summary noted some fee pages may be several years old. Page not opened.

sources.title: What are designer levels?
sources.notes: Search summary: levels reflect professionalism and skills; level reviews can be requested every 6 months if the designer has won a contest or completed a project in that period. Page not opened.

sources.title: Setting Up Hyperwallet: Required for All Designer Payouts by January 19, 2026
sources.notes: Search summary: Hyperwallet (a PayPal service) is the exclusive designer payout provider from 19 Jan 2026; designers choose their country during setup and options vary by region. Canada not named. Page not opened.

sources.title: Academic study of 99designs contests (AAAI proceedings)
sources.notes: Search summary: analysis of about 38,000 contests found a large portion of designers unable to win a single contest, with a few designers winning consistently. PDF not opened.

sources.title: Design Competition Model Is Working For 99designs, Especially In Asia
sources.notes: Search summary (older article): for every designer paid, hundreds of others aren't; contests can draw hundreds to a thousand entries. Page not opened.

sources.title: 99designs reviews (Trustpilot)
sources.notes: Anecdotal: a March 2026 client reviewer said most submitted designs looked AI-generated; the company replied that third-party material is not allowed and it has detection systems. About 1,549 reviews. Page not opened.

sources.title: 99designs Pricing 2026: How Much Does Their Talent Cost?
sources.notes: Third-party (competitor) article: logo contests Bronze US$249, Silver US$399, Gold US$799, Platinum US$1,050. The 'winner gets roughly 60%' estimate came from a related critical review on the same site and is unverified. Page not opened.

sources.title: Graphic Designer in Ontario (job prospects)
sources.notes: Search summary: outlook Very limited for graphic designers and illustrators (NOC 52120) in Ontario 2025–2027 due to employment decline; 34% self-employed vs 15% average; national wage range $20.00–$52.88/h (median $31.25) per a related wages page. Page not opened.
